issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix
issues.detail: PR's stated purpose is fixing state reuse, yet no test calls Sort() twice on the same Sorter to lock in the fix or asserts len(s.stack)==0 and len(s.state)==0 after iteration. Without it the next refactor silently reintroduces the bug. Add a regression test.

issues.description: Sorted-marker placement change on early yield=false is an undocumented semantic shift
issues.detail: Previously s.state[k]=sorted ran unconditionally after pop; now only when yield returns true. On caller bail the node is never marked sorted. Deferred clear makes this safe, but the contract for partial iteration is silent. Document that partial iteration discards progress and justify the change in the commit message.

issues.description: Three independent changes squashed into one diff
issues.detail: The patch collapses working/walking into one state, fixes the s.stack[0:] no-op via clear() + s.stack[:0], and moves the sorted-marker inside the yield branch. Each is a separate bug with separate reasoning. Squashing them defeats bisect and complicates review. Split into three commits.

issues.description: Sorter reuse contract is not written down
issues.detail: The PR effectively promises Sorter is reusable after each completed Sort, but no spec comment states preconditions, postconditions, or behavior under reentrant-panic and partial iteration. The state machine over the merged walking/sorted values is also undocumented. Add a short ADT spec comment on the Sorter type.

issues.description: Updated comment introduces two typos in load-bearing documentation
issues.detail: The rewritten comment says 'visisted' instead of 'visited' and 'if its' instead of 'if it's'. This comment is now the de-facto contract for the state field; typos invite readers to skim past it. Fix the spelling.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is directionally correct: collapsing working/walking into one state, fixing the s.stack[0:] no-op, and moving cleanup into a defer all tighten the Sorter ADT. But the work is under-documented and under-tested for a PR whose stated purpose is fixing state reuse. The biggest gaps are a missing regression test that calls Sort() twice, an undocumented semantic shift in the sorted-marker placement on early yield=false, three independent fixes squashed into one commit, and a missing written spec for the reusable-Sorter contract. Two typos in the load-bearing comment round out a clean NEEDS-WORK verdict.
